content.title: What is the Mercy Rule and how does it work in the World Baseball Classic 2026?
content.text: The World Baseball Classic 2026 - the premier international tournament for national baseball teams - is not always played over the full nine innings. In certain situations, games can end early due to a rule known as the Mercy Rule, a mechanism designed to prevent excessively lopsided scores.To watch this video, agree to share video information with third partiesAgree|More infoAlthough the rule is common in international and amateur tournaments, it is also part of the World Baseball Classic regulations and has already affected several games in the 2026 edition of the tournament.What is the Mercy Rule?The Mercy Rule allows a game to end early when the run difference becomes too large, with the goal of avoiding unbalanced contests and protecting teams - especially pitchers - in a short and intense tournament.In the World Baseball Classic, two main scenarios apply:15-run lead after 5 innings10-run lead after 7 inningsIf either of these conditions is met, the game is officially called immediately, even if there are still innings left to play.This means a game can officially end in the fifth or seventh inning.Why the rule exists in the World Baseball ClassicUnlike the regular season in Major League Baseball, the World Baseball Classic has several unique characteristics:A short and intense scheduleLimited pitching staffsTeams with varying competitive levelsThe rule helps protect pitching arms and avoid unnecessary wear and tear when the outcome of a game is already essentially decided.Additionally, in the group stage each team plays only a few games, so managing pitchers carefully is critical to advancing.Examples in the 2026 World Baseball ClassicThe rule has already come into play in several games during the tournament.One of the most notable examples was Japan's 13-0 victory over Chinese Taipei, highlighted by a Shohei Ohtani grand slam, in a game that ended in the seventh inning due to the run differential.It was also applied when the Dominican Republic defeated the Netherlands 12-1, ending the game after seven innings.Overall, the rule has been used multiple times throughout the history of the tournament, reflecting the competitive gaps that can sometimes exist between powerhouse national teams and emerging baseball programs.Does the rule apply in every round?Not exactly.The Mercy Rule only applies during the group stage of the World Baseball Classic. Once the knockout rounds begin - quarterfinals, semifinals and the final - games must be played to completion, regardless of the score.This ensures that the most important games in the tournament are decided under traditional baseball conditions.
